newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African union seeks security at Amplats.
newsitem.headline: S.African union seeks security at Amplats.

text.p: South Africa's National Union of Mineworkers on Wednesday pushed for tough security measures to be adopted at Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd's Rustenburg mine, where three of its members have been killed.

NUM spokesman George Molebatsi said after a meeting with mine management that union leaders had called on the company to appoint an independent security firm to patrol the workers' hostels and undertake regular weapons searches.
The union also asked for immediate search operations by the police and army in a village and squatter settlement near the mine, to be followed by random raids over the next six months.
In addition, Molebatsi said, the NUM wanted to commission armed security for its own leadership on the mine.

"Our argument is that the management should provide a good and safe working environment, and in terms of that there should be joint responsibility from ourselves and all the other stakeholders," he told Reuters.
"The NUM will take drastic steps against its members who transgress the policies of the union, which has always stood against violence."

A memorial service was held on Wednesday for the union's branch secretary at Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd Rudwell Daile, who was killed last Wednesday by unknown assailants, and another NUM official, Eric Rixi, who was shot dead at the weekend.

Molebatsi said the union had learned on Wednesday of another miner's death. He said Aaron Mfanta, also a NUM member at the mine who was off duty at the weekend, was was shot at and hacked with pangas in the Tabamkulu district of the former Transkei.

"It is a major concern to us that this happened away from the mine... We hear from our people on the ground that the rivals to the union say our members will be killed at work and in their homes. NUM is looking for visible police action."

Molebatsi said the management at the mine had come up with its own proposals which included the setting up of a satellite police station and army barracks as well as a reward for information which led to arrests and successful prosecutions.
The company had also suggested a peace summit involving all affected parties, he said.
The mine's management is expected to issue a statement later this week.
Moletbatsi said further meetings were likely to be held between the union and mine management, but gave no timeframe.

The Rustenburg platinum mine, the world's largest, has been plagued by a long-running dispute over union representation. It was hit late last month by a two-day wildcat strike affecting 15 percent of production.
Rusplats produced 690,000 ounces of platinum in the six months to December 1996.
